study_identification_part.si4_title: Atypical Brain Asymmetry in Autism: A Candidate for Clinically Meaningful Stratification

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Model individual deviations in gray matter hemispheric laterality across age using normative modeling to characterize heterogeneous asymmetry patterns in autism and test their associations with clinical features (e.g., language delay).

rci1_dataset_name.reason: The study explicitly states that the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) was used as the primary dataset, comprising 233 neurotypical control subjects for the normative model, and ABIDE I and II were used as a replication dataset with 691 neurotypical subjects.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: We leveraged the EU-AIMS (European Autism Interventions - A Multicentre Study for Developing New Medications) Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP)... dataset comprising 352 individuals with autism and 233 neurotypical control subjects as well as a replication dataset from ABIDE (Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange) (513 individuals with autism, 691 neurotypical subjects)
rci1_dataset_name.location: Main text, Abstract section and Methods section; Floris2021.pdf.md lines 11-12, 33-36, 40-41

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD shows individualized patterns of both extreme right- and leftward laterality deviations. Language delay relates to greater rightward deviations; core ASD severity relates more to leftward deviations. Results are robust and replicate in ABIDE.
